job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 4: return to the best-known ranking (iteration 2's shrunk hist_gbdt on impute:none) but move the one axis still unmeasured within it — mid-range capacity plus a slightly heavier positive weight — since the bar is unreachable and the job is now to maximise validation balanced_accuracy. Concretely: hist_gbdt with learning_rate 0.04, max_iter 400, max_leaf_nodes 16, max_depth 4, l2_regularization 5.0, min_samples_leaf 40, max_features 0.7, early_stopping false (all 5,026 train rows), class_weight {\"0\":1,\"1\":6}. Preprocessing stays impute:none / scale:false / no missingness columns, identical to iteration 2, so the row is attributable to the capacity+weight change alone. Iteration 2 sat at balanced_accuracy 0.7766 with recall 0.7681 vs specificity 0.7850 and cut_headroom 0.0083 — the cut is already essentially optimal for that ranking, so the only thing that can raise the score is a slightly better ranking (roc_auc 0.8583, best-cut 0.7849 are the numbers to beat) at a capacity between the memorising point (attempt 1: leaves 31 / depth 6 / gap 0.2721) and the heavily shrunk point (attempt 2: leaves 8 / depth 3 / gap 0.0608). An explicit weight of 6 (just under the 5.07 'balanced' ratio's effect at the shifted operating point, nudged up) keeps recall and specificity within a couple of points of each other so the near-optimal cut is preserved while the ranking is tested.",

      "0": 1.0,

    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Differs from iteration 3 in family (extra_trees → hist_gbdt) and pipeline (impute median + missing_count true → impute none, no missingness columns), i.e. back to iteration 2's pipeline. Differs from iteration 2 (the current best) in capacity and imbalance lever: max_leaf_nodes 8→16, max_depth 3→4, learning_rate 0.03→0.04, max_iter 300→400, l2_regularization 10.0→5.0, min_samples_leaf 60→40, max_features 0.5→0.7, class_weight 'balanced'→{\"0\":1,\"1\":6}. Differs from iteration 1 by being far more regularised (lr 0.06→0.04, leaves 31→16, depth 6→4, l2 1.0→5.0, min_samples_leaf added, max_features 0.7) and by the explicit weight map. No configuration on record has this capacity point.",
  "rationale": "The two attempts inside hist_gbdt bracket the capacity axis at its extremes: attempt 1 memorised (train_val_gap 0.2721, best-cut 0.7810) and attempt 2 was heavily shrunk (gap 0.0608, best-cut 0.7849). Both landed near best-cut 0.78, but the interior of that axis — moderate depth<path> with substantial shrinkage and feature subsampling — has not been fitted, and it is the only place a ranking gain of the size the ranking axis actually offers (0.002–0.008 roc_auc per move on record) can still be found. Family swapping is spent: extra_trees, a maximally different induction scheme, produced a *lower* best-cut (0.7697) and a resolved -0.0356 regression, so a third family is not the move. The operating point is also spent — cut_headroom 0.0083 at iteration 2 means the default cut is already within a percentage point of the best any cut of that ranking allows — so class_weight here is set only to hold recall≈specificity at the new ranking rather than to buy score; the explicit {\"0\":1,\"1\":6} is a single small step around the 5.07 class ratio so specificity does not collapse the way an aggressive weight would. impute:none is kept because hist_gbdt splits on NaN natively and the card shows 60 columns with missing values (worst 0.7852); imputing to the median there was one of the two owners of iteration 3's regression, and the missingness-column levers have no established size on this file, so they are left off to keep this row attributable. The bar 0.8882 requires KS 0.7764 against 0.5698 on the best ranking on record and is not reachable with these 119 columns; the aim of this attempt is the best validation balanced_accuracy obtainable, i.e. beating 0.7766.",

  "iteration": 4
}
